summary: Cross-cloud diagnostic bridge blocked by new org-tag enforcement and IAM Condition mismatch
description:
Issue summary: An internal ephemeral access bridge used by SRE to assume AWS diagnostic roles from GCP CI runners is failing with AccessDenied errors after the org moved to tag-enforcement for resource tagging. Impact: SRE cannot perform cross-cloud live debug of customer Dedicated clusters or run ephemeral cost-inspection jobs. Root cause appears to be a combination of an AWS Organizations SCP that denies AssumeRole when required tag keys are missing and a GCP IAM Condition on the service account that injects a tag attribute which does not match the AWS expectation.

This ticket tracks investigation and mitigation steps for restoring safe, auditable cross-cloud assume-role flows for ephemeral diagnostics.
impact: SRE debugging and some automated maintenance jobs that rely on cross-cloud assume-role (GCP -> AWS) are blocked. Potential delayed incident response for dedicated customer clusters in us-west-2. No external customer-facing API errors observed yet, but operational risk elevated.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From a GCP CI runner with the diagnostic service account: gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=$KEY
2) Generate STS token and call AWS STS: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ephemeral-diagnostic --role-session-name test --duration-seconds 900
3) Observe: An AccessDenied with message 'Caller does not have required tags' or 'Condition check failed'.
Command output and STS request/response captured in logs below.

investigation_notes: 03-10 09:20 — Confirmed failure reproduces from staging runner and prod runner using identical flow.

03-10 10:05 — Pulled AWS Organizations SCPs: new tag enforcement SCP added 2026-03-08 requiring redwood:team and redwood:owner on cross-account assume-role. SCP denies AssumeRole when tags absent or mismatched.
03-10 11:00 — Reviewed GCP-to-AWS bridge code: bridge populates tags based on GCP service account attributes. Current mapping only sets redwood:env and redwood:job-id, not redwood:team.

03-10 14:15 — Hypothesis: Org policy enforcement on AWS is stricter than the bridge mapping; missing tag causes deny. Also found a GCP IAM Condition on the diagnostic service account that explicitly allows impersonation only when attribute 'team' == 'infra', but that attribute is not propagated into AWS tags.
03-11 09:40 — Tested local patch to include static redwood:team tag in bridge token; temporary test succeeded (AssumeRole returned credentials).
03-11 13:05 — Need coordination: changing bridge to include tags requires security review and update to logging to ensure tag provenance is auditable.
timeline: 2026-03-10 — Incident created by Aisha after on-call observed failed diagnostic run in #sre-support.
2026-03-10 10:30 — Notified Cloud Infra; triage meeting scheduled at 11:00.
2026-03-10 14:30 — Reproduced failure; confirmed SCP addition on 2026-03-08 as likely trigger.
2026-03-11 09:00 — Implemented temporary patch on a staging bridge instance to inject redwood:team for testing.
2026-03-11 11:00 — Patch validated; security requested design doc for permanent change.
2026-03-12 08:45 — This ticket updated with proposed remediation options and owners.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary bridge patch in staging to include required tags while security reviews permanent approach. Long term options: (A) enhance bridge mapping to derive 'redwood:team' from GCP service account attribute and add audit logging; (B) introduce intermediary tag-assertion Lambda in AWS with strict provenance checks; (C) update org SCP to allow specific service account ARNs to assume without tags for a transition window. Next step: decision required from Cloud Security + Infra.

Lina Huang (Cloud Security, 2026-03-10 16:00): Security flagged that any change which auto-injects 'redwood:team' must be auditable and backed by service-account-to-team mapping. Creating a small design task.\n
